# not-validated: a pawprint charm's mode budget is never checked; the seat and the arms can exceed it

**Defect.** A pawprint charm's mode budget is never enforced. The model seat, and every zero-model arm, can choose a
set of modes whose pawprints exceed the card's budget, and the engine resolves it. This breaks "the engine validates
every option": an illegal play is possible.

**Where.**
- `forge-overlay/.../spike/LlmSpikeGui.java`: the `allowRepeat` branch of the modal-spell hook (`decideModesRepeat` and
  its caller near the `MODAL SPELL — choose mode(s)` prompt).
- `PuzzleArms.repeatModes` (PR #414) for the arms.
- `AnswerTool.Spec.repeat` bounds only the count.

**Evidence (engine source, pinned checkout).**
- `CharmEffect.java` mentions `Pawprint` only in the description text (lines 117 and 183-184: "{P} worth of modes").
  `makeChoices` / `chainAbilities` chain whatever the controller returns.
- The budget is enforced only by the controllers: `PlayerControllerHuman.java` 2002-2006 and 2024 remove modes whose
  pawprints exceed what is left, and `CharmAi` does the same. The harness replaces both.
- Six cards in the pool have `Pawprint$`: Season of Gathering, Season of Loss, Season of the Bold, Season of the Burrow,
  Season of Weaving, and Hela's Arcanum (each `CharmNum$ 5`, `MinCharmNum$ 0`, modes costing 1 to 3 pawprints).
- Example: Season of Loss with five picks of its 3-pawprint mode is 15 pawprints against a budget of 5. Neither the seat
  path nor the arm path refuses it.
- Found by the pr-review of PR #414 (#269 item 2). The defect predates that PR.

**What should have happened.** As `PlayerControllerHuman` does: the modes offered, or accepted, sum to at most the
`Pawprint$` budget.
- For the seat: offer only the modes that fit what is left, or validate the chosen multiset and ask again.
- For the arms: draw within the budget.
- One check, used by both branches.

**Reproduce.** A unit test in `GoldenChecksTest`: cast Season of Loss with a scripted model that answers the 3-pawprint
mode five times, and assert that the chosen modes' pawprints sum to at most 5 (today they sum to 15). Rung a; no game
needed.

**Detector gap.** None of the sheet's scripts reads chosen modes against a budget.

# Puzzle prover follow-ups left by the PR #268 review

The reviews of PR #268 found these LOW issues and left them for later. Each one is small and separate from the others.

- [ ] **`PuzzleAcceptance` accepts a misspelled counter name.**
  - `forge-overlay/.../spike/PuzzleAcceptance.java`, the `counters` condition.
  - `CounterType.getType` creates a custom counter type for any name, so a typo like `P1p1` reads 0 without any warning. As a result, `counters ... P1p1 = 0` is always accepted.
  - This contradicts the class contract: "a line it cannot read is refused".
  - Fix: check the name against `CounterEnumType` and the keyword counters in `parseLine`.
- [ ] **The search arm draws repeatable modes as ordered tuples of full size.**
  - `LlmSpikeGui.java` `decideModesRepeat`, search arm.
  - The arm always draws exactly `min(num, 8)` modes, with replacement, in order. For "up to N", the prover never tries fewer modes, for either seat. It also branches over orderings that are the same choice.
  - Fix: for `Search`, draw a count in `[min, num]`, then a multiset.
- [ ] **A lethal tap source can still pay before an "unpreferred" source.**
  - `ComputerUtilMana.java`: since epoch 65, a lethal source goes into `useLastManaSources`.
  - That list also holds sources whose cost sacrifices another permanent. It is sorted by `sortByEvaluateCreature`, which ranks creatures, so the order between two non-creatures is arbitrary.
  - Fix: append lethal sources to their own list after `useLastManaSources`, and add a golden check with such a source.
- [ ] **`PuzzleSearch`'s `gaveUp` path has no test.**
  - `PuzzleSearch.java`: removing `!gaveUp &&` keeps every test green.
  - The flag only feeds report fields (`search_exhausted`, `uniqueness_exhausted`), never a verdict.
  - About 5000 toy configurations never reached the flaw it guards against. The only path to it needs a give-up at two levels at once.

## Defect
The state lists Forge's internal "Keyword Effects" object as a card in a player's command zone, with a handle, as if
it were a card the seat could inspect, play or target.

## What happened
Found by the rules probe's engine labeller (PR #359), not in a game, PR head @ 96a6500 (the observation code is
main's). On every board where the opponent controls Leyline of Sanctity (the labeller's `opp-leyline` variant, e.g.

```
OPP [Opponent] life 20 | ...
  board: Leyline of Sanctity [untapped] @12
  command: Keyword Effects @13
```

The labeller first offered `@13` as a card to cast, play and target (now excluded there with `Card.isImmutable()`).

## What should have happened
"Keyword Effects" is an engine effect object that holds keywords granted to a player, here the player hexproof
Leyline gives: `forge-game/src/main/java/forge/game/player/Player.java` (about line 3642) builds it with
`setGamePieceType(GamePieceType.EFFECT)`, `setName("Keyword Effects")`, `setImageKey(ImageKeys.HIDDEN_CARD)` and adds
it to the command zone. It is not a card. The state either leaves it out of the command line or says what it is
("you have hexproof (Leyline of Sanctity)"), and never gives it a handle a seat could name.

## Evidence
The state lines above, from the labeller's rows for that board (export of `RulesProbeLabelExport`). Not checked:
whether the solver's own command line shows it when an effect grants the solver a keyword (the same `zoneList` call).

## Where
`forge-overlay/forge-gui-desktop/src/main/java/forge/spike/SeatObservation.java` about lines 1091 and 1106:
`zoneList(viewer.getCardsIn(ZoneType.Command), ...)` and `zoneList(opp.getCardsIn(ZoneType.Command), ...)` list every
object in the command zone; effect objects (`Card.isImmutable()`) other than the puzzle's goal are not filtered or
described.

A unit test in `SeatObservationTest`: `bareGame()`, `Leyline of Sanctity` on the rival's battlefield (so the engine
creates the Keyword Effects object; confirm with `rival.getCardsIn(ZoneType.Command)`), render the solver's snapshot,

The state has no "Keyword Effects" entry with a handle; if the granted keyword is shown, it is shown as the player's
("hexproof"), and `AskContract` still passes.

## Detector gap
`match_review.py` LEAK looks for engine ids and placeholders; an engine effect object's name ("Keyword Effects",
"Effect") listed as a card is the same kind of leak and could be added to it.

# A Disturb cast whose back face is an Aura is never on the play menu

## Defect
A Disturb cast whose back face is an Aura is never on the play menu: the menu's target check counts the Aura's
"enchant" targets while the card is still its front face in the graveyard, finds none, and hides a legal cast.

## What happened
Found by the rules probe's engine labeller (PR #359, `RulesProbeLabelExport`), not in a game: board
`eval/puzzles/rules-pilot/authored-drafts/y_105.pzl`, base variant, built from the PR head @ 96a6500 (the menu code
is main's). The solver has Grizzly Bears, three blue mana floating and Lantern Bearer in its graveyard. The proposal
`cast @2 (Disturb)` (and `cast @2 face "Lanterns' Lift"`) is refused by the propose checker with
`ILLEGAL (target): it has no legal target now.`, because the menu (`enumeratePlayOptions`) offers no play of Lantern
Bearer at all. A menu seat on that board cannot make the play either. That play is the board's own solution.

## What should have happened
Lantern Bearer (`forge-gui/res/cardsfolder/l/lantern_bearer_lanterns_lift.txt`): `K:Disturb:2 U`, "You may cast this
card from your graveyard transformed for its disturb cost"; its back face Lanterns' Lift is
`Types:Enchantment Aura`, `K:Enchant:Creature`, "Enchanted creature gets +1/+1 and has flying". With {2}{U}
available and a creature on the battlefield, casting it by Disturb is legal (CR 702.146a; an Aura spell targets the
object it will enchant, CR 303.4a). The menu offers `CAST Lantern Bearer (Disturb)`, its target ask lists Grizzly
Bears and the opponent's Wall of Stone, and a proposal of it is accepted.

## Evidence
A scratch probe on the PR head (an empty `bareGame(MAIN1)`, three Islands and Grizzly Bears on the battlefield,
Lantern Bearer in the graveyard), printing each spell of the card and its alternative costs through the menu's own
gates:

```
disturb: menu plays of Lantern Bearer: NONE
sa=[Lantern Bearer - Creature 1 / 1] way=null playable=false payable=true targets=- offerable=false
sa=[Disturb {2}{U} (You may cast this card ...)] way=Disturb playable=true payable=true targets=0 of min 1 offerable=false
```

The Disturb ability is playable and payable; `TargetRestrictions.getAllCandidates` gives 0 candidates for a minimum
of 1, so `offerable` returns false. The labeller labels the cast "ILLEGAL (target)" in 12 positions of that board
(named as Disturb, as "alternative" and as the face, on four variants: `python3 eval/rules_probe.py count <items>
--label illegal --name "Lantern Bearer" --category target`, PR #359); its hand audit of 60 negatives found two of
them (note `eval/research/2026-11-05-rules-probe.md` section 9.3).

## Where
`forge-overlay/forge-gui-desktop/src/main/java/forge/spike/LlmSpikeGui.java` `offerable` (about line 10110), the loop
"Skip a play a part of which has no legal target": `targetCandidates(part, tr).size() < part.getMinTargets()` with
`targetCandidates` (about line 1399) calling `tr.getAllCandidates(sa, false)`. For a transformed cast from the
graveyard the restrictions are evaluated against the card's current (front, creature) state, so "a creature this Aura
can enchant" matches nothing. Not confirmed which part of `getAllCandidates` drops them; the propose checker's
`proposalRejection` -> `costOrTarget` runs the same count and gives the "no legal target" sentence.

## Reproduce without the game
1. A unit test in `ProposeActionsTest` (or `PuzzleSetupTest` with the board above): `bareGame(PhaseType.MAIN1)`,
   three `Island` and `Grizzly Bears` on the solver's battlefield, `Lantern Bearer` in its graveyard, `seat(...)`;
   assert that `enumeratePlayOptions(me, true, true).spells` holds a spell whose host is Lantern Bearer and whose
   `castWay` is "Disturb". It fails on main today (no play of the card).
2. The labeller on the one board: from `$FORGE_HOME/forge-gui-desktop`, run `org.testng.TestNG -testclass
   forge.spike.RulesProbeLabelExport` with `-Dharness.probe.boards=eval/puzzles/rules-pilot/authored-drafts/y_105.pzl
   -Dharness.probe.variants=base -Dharness.probe.out=/tmp/y105.jsonl` (its class comment has the full command), then
   look for the row `"cost":"Disturb"`: `"label":"illegal","category":"target"` today.

## Fixed when
On that board the menu offers the Disturb cast, its target ask lists Grizzly Bears (and Wall of Stone), the cast
resolves as Lanterns' Lift attached to the chosen creature, and the proposal `cast @<Lantern Bearer> (Disturb)
targeting @<Bears>` is accepted. The unit test above passes; the labeller labels the Disturb row legal.
